audit.process: Delivering a change in comptoir: three services, one contract (AI instrumentation of the repository: AGENTS.md)
audit.scope: fixtures/repos/microservices/repo/ — AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, services/billing/AGENTS.md, tools/, shared/bus.py, the test_contract.py files, .github/
audit.author: author of the fixture: regression baseline of the grader, not a measurement of the skill

elements.finding: Short file, justified, dated, almost entirely guarded by tools. One rule in it is declared enforced by a test that covers only one side of it: "a contract change is additive". Two lines are to be removed, the rest is kept as is.
elements.target: The additive rule is marked (unverified) as long as no test replays a consumer; the target is a guardrail, not one more sentence.
elements.check: A PR that renames a field of contracts/events/order.created.json in the schema and in orders fails the CI.

elements.finding: One-line stub to AGENTS.md: single source.
Six lines, two rules specific to the service, justified, dated, guarded by test_ledger.py, consistent with the root. Loaded on demand: that is its place.
Tested validator; an unknown keyword raises an error instead of passing silently, including where no instance goes.
Check of the imports between services, tested, structured output with --json, exit code, blocking on every PR. It carries a rule that AGENTS.md still declares unverified.
elements.target: Nothing in the tool; it is AGENTS.md that must cite it.

elements.finding: The test bus delivers every event twice by default: any consumer test is a redelivery test. It is the real guardrail of the idempotence rule.
Does what it says: what orders publishes and answers conforms to the strict schema. It does not guard the additive rule, and it is not its job to do so.
Guards the numbering with no gap and the frozen invoice.
Two jobs, both blocking, with no path filter and no continue-on-error: everything runs on every PR.
elements.target: Nothing to remove; this is where the guardrail of the additive rule will land.

process_leaks.rule: A contract change is additive: nothing is renamed, removed or retyped
process_leaks.if_skipped: A field renamed in the schema and in the provider passes all the tests and the CI; the readers of the old name break in production. Already happened on 12 May 2026.
process_leaks.guard_tool: A test that replays a consumer against what the provider really publishes; failing that, the test events of billing and of notifications validated against the schema, and a check that compares each schema to the one on main.

guarded_rules.rule: What a service publishes or answers is declared in the contract, strict schemas
A service never imports another service's code
Invoice numbers follow one another with no gap; an issued invoice is frozen

removals.text: An event weighs less than 64 KB, envelope included: no file and no export in an event, publish its address.
removals.question: The rule dates from October 2024 and relies on the broker's shared plan; docs/operations.md says the broker has been a dedicated cluster since March 2025. Does the 64 KB limit still exist?

removals.text: Before opening a PR, run `grep -rnE "^(from|import) services\." services/ shared/ tools/` and review each line by hand.

remediation.action: Mark the additive rule (unverified) in AGENTS.md:17, then write the guardrail: a test that replays a consumer, or the comparison of the schemas to those on main.
remediation.check: Renaming a field in the schema and in orders fails the CI.

remediation.action: Replace (unverified) with "Enforced by: tools/check_imports.py" on AGENTS.md:19 and remove the review with grep of line 20.
remediation.check: harness rules counts the import rule among the guarded rules.

remediation.action: Ask the owner the question of the 64 KB limit; remove AGENTS.md:21 if they confirm it disappeared with the former broker.
remediation.check: Owner's answer recorded in the PR.

unverified: The CI and docker-compose.yml were not run.
The consumers outside the repository (comptoir-export, data warehouse) cannot be read from here.
The README cites tools/replay.py, which does not exist: outside the scope of the instructions, reported to the owner.
